entities.title: Exit statuses
entities.summary: zazzle git message exits 0 when saved and 1 when cancelled or failed, which git reads as go on or abort; zazzle git commit returns git commit's status; forwarded commands return git's own.
consumers: git, running the editor as core.editor, GIT_EDITOR or GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR
guarantees: message: 0 saved; 1 cancelled, interrupted by a signal, or failed (file too large, not UTF-8, no terminal, write error); 2 for a wrong command line; 0 for help.
commit: git commit's exit status; 1 when cancelled, when there is nothing to commit, or when a git step before the commit fails; 0 for help.
Any other command: git's own exit status, since zazzle-git replaces itself with git; 127 only if git cannot be started.
help and version exit 0.

entities.title: The commit draft and saved marks
entities.summary: zazzle git commit keeps the message in ZAZZLE_COMMIT_MSG and the file marks in ZAZZLE_COMMIT_FILES inside the repository's git directory until a commit succeeds.
consumers: The next run of zazzle git commit in the same repository
A developer who wants to recover a message after a failed commit
entities.definition: Both paths come from `git rev-parse --git-path`. ZAZZLE_COMMIT_MSG is the message text, git comments included, handed to `git commit --cleanup=strip -F`. ZAZZLE_COMMIT_FILES is JSON: {"head": the HEAD commit id when saved (empty before the first commit), "marks": {path: one of skip, add, ignore, remove, delete}}.
guarantees: The draft is written only when none exists, from the last message (--amend) or commit.template, then guidance comments and the branch.
The marks are written after Ctrl+S, before any file is staged.
Both files are removed only when git commit exits 0; a cancel or a failing commit keeps them.
Saved marks are applied only when their head equals the current HEAD, and only to files that are still changed.
entities.compatibility: Nothing versions the marks format; an unreadable file or an unknown mark name is ignored.

entities.title: Program names and version line
entities.summary: The package builds zazzle-git, zazzle-git-commit and zazzle-git-commit-message-editor, and `zazzle-git --version` prints `zazzle-git VERSION` followed by git's version.
consumers: The zazzle invoker, which execs zazzle-git for `zazzle git`
The release workflow, bottle.sh and formula.sh, which ship the three binaries
The formula's test block and CI's smoke test, which run zazzle-git --version
guarantees: zazzle-git takes the arguments that followed `zazzle git`.
zazzle-git-commit takes the same arguments as `zazzle git commit`, and zazzle-git-commit-message-editor the same as `zazzle git message`.
entities.compatibility: Renaming a binary breaks the invoker's exec, the release packaging and brew test.

entities.title: The one-time offer to become git's editor
entities.summary: The first interactive zazzle git commit asks once whether to set the global core.editor to `zazzle git message`, and records in the global git config that it asked.
consumers: A developer running zazzle git commit for the first time
git, which then opens zazzle git message for git commit, rebase -i and merge
entities.definition: Before the editor opens, zazzle git commit reads core.editor and the global key zazzle.editorOffered. If core.editor does not already name zazzle git message, z git message or zazzle-git-commit-message-editor, and zazzle.editorOffered is not true, it prints the question with the exact git config command on /dev/tty and reads one line: y or yes runs `git config --global core.editor 'zazzle git message'`; anything else changes nothing. Either way it sets zazzle.editorOffered to true.
guarantees: The question is asked at most once per user (global git config), whatever the answer.
Nothing is changed without a yes; the default answer is no.
It is never asked with -m, -F, -C or --no-edit, nor without a terminal.
The help texts of zazzle git, zazzle git commit and zazzle git message show the same command and how to undo it.
entities.compatibility: Removing zazzle.editorOffered from the global git config makes the next zazzle git commit ask again.

entities.title: The commit message prompt file
entities.summary: The agent's instructions come from the nearest .zazzle/commit-message-prompt.md, looked for from the folder the command started in upwards to the home folder, or from built-in instructions.
consumers: A developer or a repository that wants its own commit message style
The agent CLI, which receives the instructions at the start of the prompt
entities.definition: Plain text, used whole as the prompt's instructions. find_prompt checks <folder>/.zazzle/commit-message-prompt.md in the starting folder and each parent, stopping at the home folder; from a folder outside the home folder it searches every parent up to the root, then ~/.zazzle/commit-message-prompt.md. The prompt is the instructions, then `Branch:`, the last ten commit subjects and `Changes:` with the marked files' changes (zazzle git commit) or the staged diff (git's editor).
guarantees: The nearest file wins; files above the home folder are not read for folders inside it.
A missing, unreadable or blank file gives the built-in instructions (DEFAULT_PROMPT).
zazzle git commit searches from the folder it was started in, not the repository root it moves to.

entities.title: The remembered agent and effort
entities.summary: Ctrl+N and Ctrl+E save the chosen agent and effort in the global git config as zazzle.agent and zazzle.effort, which the next editor reads.
consumers: The next zazzle git commit or zazzle git message for a commit message
A developer who sets or removes the keys with git config --global
entities.definition: zazzle.agent is claude, codex or gemini; zazzle.effort is one of that agent's levels (claude: low, medium, high, xhigh, max; codex: low, medium, high) or empty for gemini. Both are written together, with `git config --global`, whenever either key is cycled.
guarantees: A saved agent that is not on PATH is ignored and the first agent found is used.
A saved effort the chosen agent does not have is replaced by that agent's default (low; none for gemini).
Nothing is written until the developer presses Ctrl+N or Ctrl+E.

entities.title: The agent command lines
entities.summary: Each agent CLI is run with a fixed command line that reads the prompt on stdin and prints only the message.
consumers: The claude, codex and gemini CLIs on PATH
entities.definition: claude: `claude -p --tools "" --no-session-persistence --effort <effort>`. codex: `codex exec --sandbox read-only --skip-git-repo-check --ephemeral -c model_reasoning_effort=<effort> -`. gemini: `gemini --approval-mode plan -p "Write the commit message described above."`. The prompt goes to stdin, stdout is the answer, and the first non-blank stderr line is the reason shown when the exit status is not 0.
guarantees: The agent runs in its own process group, which is killed after 300 seconds, when a new run starts, or when the editor closes.
An answer wrapped in a Markdown code fence is unwrapped and trimmed; an empty answer counts as a failure.
entities.compatibility: The command lines depend on each CLI's own flags; a CLI that renames one of them makes that agent fail with its error line.
